data: First known interstellar object to visit our solar system. Detected in October 2017 by the Pan-STARRS survey three weeks after closest approach to the Sun. Its hyperbolic trajectory (eccentricity ~1.2) confirmed it originated outside the solar system. Highly elongated, dark red, and showing non-gravitational acceleration of unknown cause. Already on its way out — will not return.
ʻOumuamua had e > 1 — a hyperbolic, unbound orbit. The first confirmed interstellar object to pass through the solar system (2017).
Oumuamua's trajectory was the textbook hyperbolic conic — defined by escape velocity exceeded at every point. By the time it was discovered it was already leaving.
How stretched the orbit is — zero is a perfect circle, one is a parabolic escape.
Slice a cone four ways and you get every possible Keplerian trajectory — circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola.
